name: Furbolg
summary: Across northern Kalimdor, Furbolg tribes turn on their old allies as madness takes hold. For millennia, they lived in harmony with nature and the night elves. Now demonic corruption and lingering fel magic leave only a few tribes sane.

sections.title: Ancient Kinship
sections.body: Furbolg packs once fought beside night elves and tauren against the Burning Legion. During the War of the Ancients, ten thousand years ago, chieftain Unng Ak united the tribes. They had long revered the wild god Ursoc. After the Great Sundering, they withdrew into the northern woodlands. There, they kept peaceful ties with night elf druids and forest wardens, living simply among the wild.

sections.title: The Scourge of Madness
sections.body:
The Third War shattered the furbolgs’ quiet life. As the Burning Legion crossed Kalimdor, fel taint spread through the soil and canopy of Ashenvale and Felwood. Deeply attuned to the land, the bear-men took the corruption into themselves, and madness seized their tribes.

Wizened shamans were overthrown or silenced by bloodthirsty firebrands. These new leaders channeled fel moss, dark talismans, and corrupt alchemy. Peaceful gatherers became raiders who attack travelers and night elf settlements on sight.

sections.title: The Unbroken Line
sections.body:
Across northern Kalimdor, nearly every major tribe has fallen. The Gnarlpine dwell across Teldrassil, the Blackwood in Darkshore, and the Thistlefur and Foulweald in Ashenvale. The Deadwood and Winterfall live in the northern highlands. Yet a few still hold to their old ways.

Deep in fortified tunnels linking Felwood, Winterspring, and Moonglade, the Timbermaw guard their sanity. Wary and isolated, they defend their hold against their crazed northern kin. They fight to preserve what remains of their uncorrupted culture.

faq.q: Why are the furbolgs attacking everyone?
faq.answer: Since the Third War, lingering demonic corruption has spread through Kalimdor’s northern forests. Furbolgs are deeply attuned to nature, and the taint seeped into their minds. It drove their tribes into a paranoid, violent frenzy and displaced peaceful elders with aggressive chieftains.

faq.q: Were furbolgs always enemies of the night elves?
faq.answer: No. For thousands of years, furbolgs and night elves were peaceful neighbors and close allies. They fought together against the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients. Night elf druids kept gentle ties with tribal settlements until the recent madness took hold.

faq.q: Are there any furbolgs who are still friendly?
faq.answer: Yes. The Timbermaw keep an uncorrupted enclave in Timbermaw Hold, the crossroads tunnel system between Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring. Deeply suspicious of outsiders, they tolerate travelers who prove their enmity toward the tainted Deadwood and Winterfall tribes.

faq.q: What is wrong with the furbolgs on Teldrassil?
faq.answer: The Gnarlpine tribe on Teldrassil has fallen to fel moss, a corruption spreading through the world tree’s boughs. Under Chieftain Ursal the Mauler, the Gnarlpine abandoned their traditional villages and overran sacred places such as the Ban'ethil Barrow Den and Starbreeze Village.

faq.q: Who is behind the corruption of the Winterfall in Winterspring?
faq.answer: A satyr named Xandivious secretly manipulates the Winterfall from within their chieftain’s den. Their frenzy is sustained by Winterfall Firewater, brewed from tainted materials inside Felwood’s Deadwood Cauldron and carried north through the mountain passes.

faq.q: Can corrupted furbolgs ever be cured?
faq.answer: Night elf sentinels and druids have tried to cleanse individual tribes with moonwell waters and sacred relics. Broad recovery has proven nearly impossible. Satyrs and dark relics deepen the corruption, leaving defenders often with no choice but to cull hostile packs to protect settlements.

angles.text: For night elves, the furbolgs’ fall is a bitter tragedy. Tribes trusted as woodland allies for ten thousand years have become feral predators threatening Astranaar and Teldrassil’s sacred barrows.
Druids mourn the bear-men as kindred spirits of Ursoc. Fel taint has turned their bond with nature into a weapon, and their unrest reflects the land’s wider sickness.
The Horde sees Ashenvale’s hostile tribes as barriers to its advance. It clears aggressive packs such as the Foulweald and Thistlefur to secure supply routes and outposts along the forest fringe.
